{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABf3Fprw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhJUqmI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 191, "title": "Add optional GPU CRT shader presets for period-correct PC-98 RGB monitor presentation", "body": "## Problem and goal

The current browser UI displays the emulator's 640×400 RGBA frame directly through a 2D Canvas `putImageData` path ([`web/app.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/app.js), [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/index.html)). It is crisp and functional, but looks like modern flat digital pixels instead of an **era-appropriate PC-98 RGB CRT monitor**.

Add a **GPU-accelerated, optional CRT-style presentation shader** that recreates the subtle look of a high-quality period RGB display—not a composite/NTSC TV or VHS effect. This is a **host-side post-processing feature**; it must not change emulated VRAM, pixels provided by the core, machine timing, game CPU load or audio behavior.

## Proposed visual effects

- [ ] **Correct display aspect ratio**: for the current 640×400 PC-98 mode, present at 4:3 (a vertical stretch of ~1.2× relative to square pixels). Avoid double-applying correction; account for responsive layout, full-screen, device pixel ratio and future/display-mode differences. Use source-pixel coordinates for effects.
- [ ] **Subtle beam/scanline structure**: low-strength line-to-line luminance modulation (~5–12% as an initial tuning *range*, not a hardware-accuracy guarantee), anchored to the original emulated scanlines and stable while scaling. Do not produce harsh black stripes, shimmer, moving bands or moiré.
- [ ] **Slight analog spot softness**: gentle, primarily horizontal filter/beam profile; keep fine Japanese text, single-pixel lines and 16/256-color game artwork legible. Minimize pixel bleeding rather than blurring the entire frame.
- [ ] **Optional, very faint RGB phosphor/shadow-mask pattern**, enabled only when output pixel density is sufficient to represent it without aliasing; tune with DPI/scaling and offer off by default on small displays if needed.
- [ ] **Conservative tonal response**: optional mild gamma/contrast and restrained highlight glow (bloom). Preserve black levels, accurate palette recognition, and avoid blown-out white text.
- [ ] **Curvature as an optional *near-zero* effect**, no heavy geometry warp, no strong chromatic aberration. Do **not** add composite rainbow/fringing, NTSC noise, tape grain, VHS artifacts, dramatic flicker, or game-specific filtering.

## Implementation

1. **Implement an isolated presentation stage** using WebGL2 (or a justified broadly supported WebGL path) with a simple texture + fragment shader, while preserving the existing emulation Worker, render Worker, AudioWorklet, and bounded frame-credit/ack protocol. Do not make the emulator Worker perform the CRT filter. Render the latest incoming frame into a GPU texture with bounded allocations/copies. Manage the existing `canvas.getContext('2d')` exclusivity appropriately (e.g., separate output canvas/presenter or a safe renderer abstraction); retain keyboard/mouse focus and correct pointer coordinates.
2. Provide a **clean unfiltered mode / instant fallback** to the current 2D canvas if WebGL is unsupported, compilation fails, or context is lost. No black/blank screen or stuck transferable buffers. Handle context restoration, resize and device pixel ratio without restarting the guest or dropping input. No remote shaders, dependencies, fonts or assets unless necessary and licensing/asset audits pass.
3. Add user-selectable presets: **LCD / Original pixels (off)**, **Sharp CRT** (recommended default CRT profile), **Soft CRT**, and **Strong CRT** (still restrained). Expose a small settings UI; optionally add an Advanced panel for scanline strength, softness, mask, glow, gamma and curvature, with sensible clamped values. Preserve the user's choice locally if appropriate without storing guest/game/media content. Prefer the existing unfiltered appearance by default until visual and performance acceptance is established.
4. Keep all effects *display-only*, so screenshots/benchmark golden frames and guest data can still be captured **unfiltered**. Clarify raw vs filtered screenshots; do not treat differences in shader output as core emulation errors.
5. Preserve PC-98 legibility and color behavior across **VM and Ap profiles**: 640×400 text/Japanese glyphs, 16-color planar and 256-color PEGC graphics, palette changes, cursor/blink and dynamic modes. Check both small/integer and large/non-integer scaled display sizes.
6. Add lightweight diagnostics and A/B visual/performance checks: measure texture-upload time, GPU present time where feasible, presentation fps/latency, missed/coalesced frames, emulation guest/wall speed, and 48/44.1 kHz audio underflows, drops and tempo. Compare effect off/on in the normal production browser, including a CPU-constrained case; leave image/media captures local and publish only owned/rights-cleared test visuals.
7. Document visual rationale, supported browsers, presets/defaults, fallback behavior, any observed GPU/CPU/memory costs and known display limitations. Preserve static Pages builds at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/` and current packaging/security/license checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CRT presets visibly provide a **restrained RGB CRT look** (correct 4:3 geometry, subtle scanlines/softness; optional mask) without compromising Japanese text readability, 1-pixel UI elements or important color/palette differences.
- [ ] Users can switch between raw display and CRT presets without restarting a game, and changes do **not** modify guest framebuffer bytes, timing, disk, audio pitch/tempo or interrupt behavior.
- [ ] WebGL unavailable/context lost/failure gracefully falls back to the current working 2D presentation, with keyboard/mouse and frame buffers still functional.
- [ ] Shader work does not reduce the emulation's ability to run in real time or cause new audio gaps under representative workloads. Before/after numbers are documented; if an effect is too costly, simplify/disable it rather than sacrificing gameplay.
- [ ] No aliasing/moire or visible flicker at ordinary scales; source-space scanlines/mask scale correctly and respect reduced-motion/comfort expectations.
- [ ] Existing release-Wasm/browser/worker/audio tests, both profiles and both serving roots remain passing; add focused browser/pixel/geometry and context-loss regressions.

## Context

Earlier rendering work #142 separated CPU emulation from frame rasterization; #163/#164 set a 60 fps presentation target; #146/#172/#189 track game performance and audio capacity. This issue must **not** reintroduce an expensive CPU-side pixel-processing stage or undermine those optimizations.
